  <title>Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1>My Site About Indiana State Parks</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>
  <!-- ===== L8 · a jump link. #parks points at id="parks" further down ===== -->
  <p><a href="#parks">Skip to the comparison table</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · a classed div groups the intro. class = reusable ===== -->
  <div class="intro">
    <p>Welcome. This site is about the state parks in Indiana, which ones are worth
    the drive, and what you can actually do at each one.</p>

  <!-- ===== the hero image — relative path into the images folder ===== -->
  <img src="images/turkey-run-rocky-hollow.jpg"
       alt="A narrow sandstone canyon at Turkey Run with a wooden ladder bolted into the rock face">
  </div>

  <!-- ===== why I picked this ===== -->
  <h2>Why I picked this</h2>
  <p>My family has been going to Turkey Run since I was small, and I found out there
  are <strong>twenty-three more state parks</strong> I had never heard of. I want to
  make a page for each one I visit this year.</p>
  <p>The ones closest to Indianapolis are Fort Harrison and Shades. Both are under an
  hour, which matters when you are <em>relying on someone else to drive you</em>.</p>

  <!-- ===== what I already know ===== -->
  <h2>What I already know</h2>
  <p>Turkey Run has ladders bolted into the rock in some of the canyon trails.
  <span class="warning">Trail 3 is genuinely hard in wet weather</span> — that is not a warning
  the sign makes obvious enough.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite> —
  <a href="https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/" target="_blank">the official park
  listing</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L7 · an unordered list — order carries no meaning here ===== -->
  <h2>What to take</h2>
  <p>Nothing on this list is more important than the others, so it is unordered.</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Boots you do not mind soaking — Trail 3 crosses the creek</li>
    <li>More water than you think</li>
    <li>A paper map, because there is no signal in the gorge</li>
    <li>Cash for the gate</li>
  </ul>

  <!-- ===== what's coming ===== -->
  <h2>What's coming</h2>
  <p>Right now this is one page with no pictures and no colors. That is on purpose.
  Structure first.</p>
  <p>By the end of this unit there will be a page for each park, a table of hours and
  fees, and a form to tell me which one to visit next.</p>



  <!-- ===== L8 · id="parks" is UNIQUE on this page — the jump link's target ===== -->
  <section id="parks">
  <h2>The parks, side by side</h2>
  <table>
    <caption>Entry fees and hours at Indiana state parks, 2026</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Park</th>
        <th>Hours</th>
        <th>Entry fee</th>
        <th>Trails</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>Turkey Run</td>
        <td>7am – 11pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>11</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>Shades</td>
        <td>7am – 11pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>10</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>Fort Harrison</td>
        <td>7am – 11pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>6</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td colspan="3">Fees waived on free admission days</td>
        <td>—</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · same class, different content — that's what class is for ===== -->
  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
    <li>"Sugar Creek from the Shades overlook" by
      <a href="https://www.flickr.com/people/example">M. Okonkwo</a>,
      via <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/example/12345678">Flickr</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>


  <!-- ===== L9 · an iframe embeds someone else's page inside yours. This is the
       EMBED url from Share -> Embed a map, not the one in the address bar. ===== -->
  <section id="map">
  <h2>Where Turkey Run actually is</h2>
  <p>An hour and a half from Indianapolis, in Parke County, and the last twenty
  minutes have no signal.</p>

    src="https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html?bbox=-87.22%2C39.86%2C-87.16%2C39.91&layer=mapnik"

    loading="lazy"></iframe>

       and that is the spring semester. Labelled for what it WILL do. ===== -->
  <p><button type="button">Show me a random park</button></p>

</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1 id="top">Turkey Run State Park</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>

  <p>This is the park I actually know. Everything below is from walking it, not from
  the park website.</p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · on-page contents. A list (L7) whose links point at ids (L8) ===== -->
  <div class="contents">
    <h2>On this page</h2>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#route">Rocky Hollow, in order</a></li>
      <li><a href="#trails">Trails by difficulty</a></li>
      <li><a href="#glossary">Words the signs don't explain</a></li>
      <li><a href="#credits">Image credits</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <!-- ===== L8 · id="route" is unique — the contents list points here ===== -->
  <section id="route">
  <h2>Rocky Hollow, in order</h2>
  <p>Shuffle these and you would be walking the ladders downhill in the dark, so this
  one is ordered.</p>
  <ol>
    <li>Park at the Nature Center lot, not the inn</li>
    <li>Cross the suspension bridge over Sugar Creek</li>
    <li>Turn right into the gorge at the Trail 3 marker</li>
    <li>Climb the ladder section — both hands, no phone</li>
    <li>Follow the creek bed until it opens out at Wedge Rock</li>
    <li>Come back on Trail 5 rather than the way you came</li>
  </ol>

  </section>

  <section id="trails">
  <h2>Trails, grouped by how hard they are</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Easy
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 1 — paved, and the only one a stroller survives</li>
        <li>Trail 7 — flat, wooded, quiet on a weekday</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Moderate
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 5 — the sensible way back out of the gorge</li>
        <li>Trail 9 — long, but nothing technical</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Rugged
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 3 — ladders, creek crossings, <span class="warning">genuinely hard when wet</span></li>
        <li>Trail 10 — Bear Hollow, and usually empty for a reason</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <section id="glossary">
  <h2>Words the signs use without explaining</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt>Gorge</dt>
    <dd>A narrow canyon cut down through sandstone by the creek. Cold, and it stays
    wet days after the rain stops.</dd>

    <dt>Hemlock</dt>
    <dd>The dark evergreen growing out of the ravine walls. Left over from the last
    ice age, which is the single best fact about this park.</dd>

    <dt>Ladder section</dt>
    <dd>Steel rungs bolted straight into the rock face on Trail 3. Not optional —
    there is no way around it.</dd>
  </dl>

  </section>

  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · #top points at the id on the <h1> ===== -->
  <p><a href="#top">Back to top</a></p>

  </main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">

  <title>Contact — Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">

<body>

  <header>
    <h1>Tell me where to go next</h1>

    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>

  <p>I have been to four of Indiana's twenty-four state parks. If you know one worth
  the drive, tell me.</p>

  <!-- ===== L11 · action and method are named now and explained properly in U6.
       Nothing is submitted anywhere yet -- there is no backend until spring. ===== -->
  <form action="#" method="post">

    <!-- L11 · EVERY input gets a label, and for="" must match the input's id.
         Click the label text -- if the cursor jumps into the box, they match. -->
    <!-- L12 · required means the browser refuses to submit without it, and
         says so itself. No JavaScript written. -->
    <p>
      <label for="name">Your name</label><br>
      <input type="text" id="name" name="name"
             placeholder="First name is fine" required>
    </p>

    <!-- L12 · type="email" validates the shape AND changes the on-screen
         keyboard on a phone. type="text" does neither. -->
    <p>
      <label for="email">Email</label><br>
      <input type="email" id="email" name="email"
             placeholder="you@example.com" required>
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="visits">How many state parks have you been to?</label><br>
      <input type="number" id="visits" name="visits" min="0" max="24" value="0">
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="when">When would you go?</label><br>
      <input type="date" id="when" name="when">
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="park">Which park?</label><br>
      <select id="park" name="park">
        <option value="">-- pick one --</option>
        <option value="shades">Shades</option>
        <option value="brown-county">Brown County</option>
        <option value="clifty-falls">Clifty Falls</option>
        <option value="indiana-dunes">Indiana Dunes</option>
        <option value="other">Somewhere else</option>
      </select>
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="why">Why that one?</label><br>
      <textarea id="why" name="why" rows="5" cols="40"></textarea>
    </p>

    <!-- L12 · a radio GROUP shares one name. Different names = they all stay
         selectable at once, which is the classic radio-button bug. -->
    <fieldset>
      <legend>How far will you drive?</legend>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="near" name="distance" value="near" checked>
        <label for="near">Under an hour</label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="mid" name="distance" value="mid">
        <label for="mid">One to three hours</label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="far" name="distance" value="far">
        <label for="far">As far as it takes</label>
      </p>
    </fieldset>

    <p>
      <input type="checkbox" id="ladders" name="ladders" value="yes">
      <label for="ladders">I am fine with ladders and creek crossings</label>
    </p>

    <p><button type="submit">Send it</button></p>

  </form>

  <!-- L12 · try submitting this empty, then with a bad email. The browser
       complains on its own -- that is built-in validation, and it is a preview
       of the real validation you write in JavaScript in the spring.
       It still goes nowhere on submit. There is no backend until U6. -->

  </main>

  <footer>
    <p>Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>

  <!-- ===== L8 · a jump link. #parks points at id="parks" further down ===== -->
  <p><a href="#parks">Skip to the comparison table</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · a classed div groups the intro. class = reusable ===== -->
  <div class="intro">
    <p>Welcome. This site is about the state parks in Indiana, which ones are worth
    the drive, and what you can actually do at each one.</p>

  <!-- ===== the hero image — relative path into the images folder ===== -->
  <img src="images/turkey-run-rocky-hollow.jpg"
       alt="A narrow sandstone canyon at Turkey Run with a wooden ladder bolted into the rock face">
  </div>

  <!-- ===== why I picked this ===== -->
  <h2>Why I picked this</h2>
  <p>My family has been going to Turkey Run since I was small, and I found out there
  are <strong>twenty-three more state parks</strong> I had never heard of. I want to
  make a page for each one I visit this year.</p>
  <p>The ones closest to Indianapolis are Fort Harrison and Shades. Both are under an
  hour, which matters when you are <em>relying on someone else to drive you</em>.</p>

  <!-- ===== what I already know ===== -->
  <h2>What I already know</h2>
  <p>Turkey Run has ladders bolted into the rock in some of the canyon trails.
  <span class="warning">Trail 3 is genuinely hard in wet weather</span> — that is not a warning
  the sign makes obvious enough.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite> —
  <a href="https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/" target="_blank">the official park
  listing</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L7 · an unordered list — order carries no meaning here ===== -->
  <h2>What to take</h2>
  <p>Nothing on this list is more important than the others, so it is unordered.</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Boots you do not mind soaking — Trail 3 crosses the creek</li>
    <li>More water than you think</li>
    <li>A paper map, because there is no signal in the gorge</li>
    <li>Cash for the gate</li>
  </ul>

  <!-- ===== what's coming ===== -->
  <h2>What's coming</h2>
  <p>Right now this is one page with no pictures and no colors. That is on purpose.
  Structure first.</p>
  <p>By the end of this unit there will be a page for each park, a table of hours and
  fees, and a form to tell me which one to visit next.</p>



  <!-- ===== L8 · id="parks" is UNIQUE on this page — the jump link's target ===== -->
  <section id="parks">
  <h2>The parks, side by side</h2>
  <table>
    <caption>Entry fees and hours at Indiana state parks, 2026</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Park</th>
        <th>Hours</th>
        <th>Entry fee</th>
        <th>Trails</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>Turkey Run</td>
        <td>7am – 11pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>11</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>Shades</td>
        <td>7am – 11pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>10</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>Fort Harrison</td>
        <td>7am – 11pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>6</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td colspan="3">Fees waived on free admission days</td>
        <td>—</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · same class, different content — that's what class is for ===== -->
  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
    <li>"Sugar Creek from the Shades overlook" by
      <a href="https://www.flickr.com/people/example">M. Okonkwo</a>,
      via <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/example/12345678">Flickr</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>


  <!-- ===== L9 · an iframe embeds someone else's page inside yours. This is the
       EMBED url from Share -> Embed a map, not the one in the address bar. ===== -->
  <section id="map">
  <h2>Where Turkey Run actually is</h2>
  <p>An hour and a half from Indianapolis, in Parke County, and the last twenty
  minutes have no signal.</p>
  <iframe
    src="https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html?bbox=-87.22%2C39.86%2C-87.16%2C39.91&layer=mapnik"
    width="600" height="450"
    title="Map showing the location of Turkey Run State Park in Parke County, Indiana"
    loading="lazy"></iframe>
  <p><a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=13/39.885/-87.19" target="_blank">View a larger map</a></p>
  </section>

  <!-- ===== L9 · a button with nowhere to go yet. The behaviour is JavaScript,
       and that is the spring semester. Labelled for what it WILL do. ===== -->
  <p><button type="button">Show me a random park</button></p>

  <!-- TODO: add a page for Shades once I've been there -->
  </main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <!-- L9 · charset first. Without it, curly quotes become â€™ -->
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <!-- L9 · use the phone's real width instead of pretending to be a desktop.
       Nothing visible changes today; U3 is where this pays off. -->
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <!-- L9 · the grey line under this page in search results. One per PAGE. -->
  <meta name="description" content="Trail 3, the ladders, and what to take to Turkey Run State Park in Parke County, Indiana.">
  <title>Turkey Run — Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1 id="top">Turkey Run State Park</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>

  <p>This is the park I actually know. Everything below is from walking it, not from
  the park website.</p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · on-page contents. A list (L7) whose links point at ids (L8) ===== -->
  <div class="contents">
    <h2>On this page</h2>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#route">Rocky Hollow, in order</a></li>
      <li><a href="#trails">Trails by difficulty</a></li>
      <li><a href="#glossary">Words the signs don't explain</a></li>
      <li><a href="#credits">Image credits</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <!-- ===== L8 · id="route" is unique — the contents list points here ===== -->
  <section id="route">
  <h2>Rocky Hollow, in order</h2>
  <p>Shuffle these and you would be walking the ladders downhill in the dark, so this
  one is ordered.</p>
  <ol>
    <li>Park at the Nature Center lot, not the inn</li>
    <li>Cross the suspension bridge over Sugar Creek</li>
    <li>Turn right into the gorge at the Trail 3 marker</li>
    <li>Climb the ladder section — both hands, no phone</li>
    <li>Follow the creek bed until it opens out at Wedge Rock</li>
    <li>Come back on Trail 5 rather than the way you came</li>
  </ol>

  </section>

  <section id="trails">
  <h2>Trails, grouped by how hard they are</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Easy
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 1 — paved, and the only one a stroller survives</li>
        <li>Trail 7 — flat, wooded, quiet on a weekday</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Moderate
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 5 — the sensible way back out of the gorge</li>
        <li>Trail 9 — long, but nothing technical</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Rugged
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 3 — ladders, creek crossings, <span class="warning">genuinely hard when wet</span></li>
        <li>Trail 10 — Bear Hollow, and usually empty for a reason</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <section id="glossary">
  <h2>Words the signs use without explaining</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt>Gorge</dt>
    <dd>A narrow canyon cut down through sandstone by the creek. Cold, and it stays
    wet days after the rain stops.</dd>

    <dt>Hemlock</dt>
    <dd>The dark evergreen growing out of the ravine walls. Left over from the last
    ice age, which is the single best fact about this park.</dd>

    <dt>Ladder section</dt>
    <dd>Steel rungs bolted straight into the rock face on Trail 3. Not optional —
    there is no way around it.</dd>
  </dl>

  </section>

  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · #top points at the id on the <h1> ===== -->
  <p><a href="#top">Back to top</a></p>

  </main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <!-- L9 · charset first. Without it, curly quotes become â€™ -->
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <!-- L9 · use the phone's real width instead of pretending to be a desktop.
       Nothing visible changes today; U3 is where this pays off. -->
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <!-- L9 · the grey line under this page in search results. One per PAGE. -->
  <meta name="description" content="Who is writing these Indiana state park notes, and why.">
  <title>About me — Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L13 · the skip link. First focusable thing on the page, so a
       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing
       through it on every single page. Tab into the page to see it. ===== -->
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1>About me</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main id="main">

  <!-- ===== L8 · the same "section" class as index.html — reused, not redefined ===== -->
  <section id="who">
  <h2>Who is writing this</h2>
  <p>I am a sophomore at Warren Central and I have been to exactly <strong>three</strong>
  of Indiana's twenty-four state parks. That is the whole reason this site exists — I
  want a record of the rest.</p>

  <!-- ===== second image, different page, same folder ===== -->
  <img src="images/shades-sugar-creek.jpg"
       alt="A wooded overlook at Shades State Park looking down into Sugar Creek">

  </section>

  <section id="why">
  <h2>Why this topic</h2>
  <p>Most park websites tell you the hours and the entrance fee. <span class="warning">None of them tell
  you whether the trail is worth it.</span> That is the part I am trying to write down
  while I still remember it.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite> —
  <a href="https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/" target="_blank">the official park
  listing</a></p>

  </section>

  <section id="next">
  <h2>What's next</h2>
  <p>A page for each park I actually visit, with photos once I learn how to put them in.</p>


  </section>

  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
    <li>"Sugar Creek from the Shades overlook" by
      <a href="https://www.flickr.com/people/example">M. Okonkwo</a>,
      via <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/example/12345678">Flickr</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>


  <!-- ===== L13 · entities. The four that matter, and WHY they exist. ===== -->
  <h2>One thing that caught me out</h2>
  <p>I wanted to write about the <code><table></code> tag on this page and the
  table just disappeared. The browser was reading my example as a real tag instead of
  as text.</p>
  <p>The fix is an <strong>entity</strong> — a code that stands in for a character
  the browser would otherwise treat as HTML:</p>
  <table>
    <caption>The entities I actually needed</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>I type</th><th>The page shows</th><th>Why I need it</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td><code>&lt;</code></td><td><</td><td>otherwise it starts a tag</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&gt;</code></td><td>></td><td>otherwise it ends one</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&amp;</code></td><td>&</td><td>otherwise it starts an entity</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&copy;</code></td><td>©</td><td>not on the keyboard</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&nbsp;</code></td><td>a space that never breaks</td><td>keeps
        “7 am” on one line</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <p>The one that surprised me is <code>&amp;</code>. To write the ampersand code
  itself I have to escape the ampersand, which felt like a trick question until I
  thought about it.</p>
</main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>© 2026 — Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>
contact.html 
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="description" content="Tell me which Indiana state park to visit next.">
  <title>Contact — Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L13 · the skip link. First focusable thing on the page, so a
       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing
       through it on every single page. Tab into the page to see it. ===== -->
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>

  <header>
    <h1>Tell me where to go next</h1>

    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main id="main">

  <p>I have been to four of Indiana's twenty-four state parks. If you know one worth
  the drive, tell me.</p>

  <!-- ===== L11 · action and method are named now and explained properly in U6.
       Nothing is submitted anywhere yet -- there is no backend until spring. ===== -->
  <form action="#" method="post">

    <!-- L11 · EVERY input gets a label, and for="" must match the input's id.
         Click the label text -- if the cursor jumps into the box, they match. -->
    <!-- L12 · required means the browser refuses to submit without it, and
         says so itself. No JavaScript written. -->
    <p>
      <label for="name">Your name</label><br>
      <input type="text" id="name" name="name"
             placeholder="First name is fine" required>
    </p>

    <!-- L12 · type="email" validates the shape AND changes the on-screen
         keyboard on a phone. type="text" does neither. -->
    <p>
      <label for="email">Email</label><br>
      <input type="email" id="email" name="email"
             placeholder="you@example.com" required>
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="visits">How many state parks have you been to?</label><br>
      <input type="number" id="visits" name="visits" min="0" max="24" value="0">
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="when">When would you go?</label><br>
      <input type="date" id="when" name="when">
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="park">Which park?</label><br>
      <select id="park" name="park">
        <option value="">-- pick one --</option>
        <option value="shades">Shades</option>
        <option value="brown-county">Brown County</option>
        <option value="clifty-falls">Clifty Falls</option>
        <option value="indiana-dunes">Indiana Dunes</option>
        <option value="other">Somewhere else</option>
      </select>
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="why">Why that one?</label><br>
      <textarea id="why" name="why" rows="5" cols="40"></textarea>
    </p>

    <!-- L12 · a radio GROUP shares one name. Different names = they all stay
         selectable at once, which is the classic radio-button bug. -->
    <fieldset>
      <legend>How far will you drive?</legend>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="near" name="distance" value="near" checked>
        <label for="near">Under an hour</label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="mid" name="distance" value="mid">
        <label for="mid">One to three hours</label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="far" name="distance" value="far">
        <label for="far">As far as it takes</label>
      </p>
    </fieldset>

    <p>
      <input type="checkbox" id="ladders" name="ladders" value="yes">
      <label for="ladders">I am fine with ladders and creek crossings</label>
    </p>

    <p><button type="submit">Send it</button></p>

  </form>

  <!-- L12 · try submitting this empty, then with a bad email. The browser
       complains on its own -- that is built-in validation, and it is a preview
       of the real validation you write in JavaScript in the spring.
       It still goes nowhere on submit. There is no backend until U6. -->

  </main>

  <footer>
    <p>© 2026 — Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <!-- L9 · charset first. Without it, curly quotes become â€™ -->
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <!-- L9 · use the phone's real width instead of pretending to be a desktop.
       Nothing visible changes today; U3 is where this pays off. -->
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <!-- L9 · the grey line under this page in search results. One per PAGE. -->
  <meta name="description" content="Trail notes, entry fees, and hours for Indiana state parks, written by a student who keeps going back to Turkey Run.">
  <title>Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L13 · the skip link. First focusable thing on the page, so a
       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing
       through it on every single page. Tab into the page to see it. ===== -->
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1>My Site About Indiana State Parks</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main id="main">
  <!-- ===== L8 · a jump link. #parks points at id="parks" further down ===== -->
  <p><a href="#parks">Skip to the comparison table</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · a classed div groups the intro. class = reusable ===== -->
  <div class="intro">
    <p>Welcome. This site is about the state parks in Indiana, which ones are worth
    the drive, and what you can actually do at each one.</p>

  <!-- ===== the hero image — relative path into the images folder ===== -->
  <img src="images/turkey-run-rocky-hollow.jpg"
       alt="A narrow sandstone canyon at Turkey Run with a wooden ladder bolted into the rock face">
  </div>

  <!-- ===== why I picked this ===== -->
  <h2>Why I picked this</h2>
  <p>My family has been going to Turkey Run since I was small, and I found out there
  are <strong>twenty-three more state parks</strong> I had never heard of. I want to
  make a page for each one I visit this year.</p>
  <p>The ones closest to Indianapolis are Fort Harrison and Shades. Both are under an
  hour, which matters when you are <em>relying on someone else to drive you</em>.</p>

  <!-- ===== what I already know ===== -->
  <h2>What I already know</h2>
  <p>Turkey Run has ladders bolted into the rock in some of the canyon trails.
  <span class="warning">Trail 3 is genuinely hard in wet weather</span> — that is not a warning
  the sign makes obvious enough.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite> —
  <a href="https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/" target="_blank">the official park
  listing</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L7 · an unordered list — order carries no meaning here ===== -->
  <h2>What to take</h2>
  <p>Nothing on this list is more important than the others, so it is unordered.</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Boots you do not mind soaking — Trail 3 crosses the creek</li>
    <li>More water than you think</li>
    <li>A paper map, because there is no signal in the gorge</li>
    <li>Cash for the gate</li>
  </ul>

  <!-- ===== what's coming ===== -->
  <h2>What's coming</h2>
  <p>Right now this is one page with no pictures and no colors. That is on purpose.
  Structure first.</p>
  <p>By the end of this unit there will be a page for each park, a table of hours and
  fees, and a form to tell me which one to visit next.</p>



  <!-- ===== L8 · id="parks" is UNIQUE on this page — the jump link's target ===== -->
  <section id="parks">
  <h2>The parks, side by side</h2>
  <table>
    <caption>Entry fees and hours at Indiana state parks, 2026</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Park</th>
        <th>Hours</th>
        <th>Entry fee</th>
        <th>Trails</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>Turkey Run</td>
        <td>7 am – 11 pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>11</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>Shades</td>
        <td>7 am – 11 pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>10</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>Fort Harrison</td>
        <td>7 am – 11 pm</td>
        <td>$7</td>
        <td>6</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td colspan="3">Fees waived on free admission days</td>
        <td>—</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · same class, different content — that's what class is for ===== -->
  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
    <li>"Sugar Creek from the Shades overlook" by
      <a href="https://www.flickr.com/people/example">M. Okonkwo</a>,
      via <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/example/12345678">Flickr</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>

       EMBED url from Share -> Embed a map, not the one in the address bar. ===== -->

    src="https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html?bbox=-87.22%2C39.86%2C-87.16%2C39.91&layer=mapnik"

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <!-- L9 · charset first. Without it, curly quotes become â€™ -->
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <!-- L9 · use the phone's real width instead of pretending to be a desktop.
       Nothing visible changes today; U3 is where this pays off. -->
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <!-- L9 · the grey line under this page in search results. One per PAGE. -->
  <meta name="description" content="Trail 3, the ladders, and what to take to Turkey Run State Park in Parke County, Indiana.">
  <title>Turkey Run — Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L13 · the skip link. First focusable thing on the page, so a
       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing
       through it on every single page. Tab into the page to see it. ===== -->
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1 id="top">Turkey Run State Park</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main id="main">

  <p>This is the park I actually know. Everything below is from walking it, not from
  the park website.</p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · on-page contents. A list (L7) whose links point at ids (L8) ===== -->
  <div class="contents">
    <h2>On this page</h2>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#route">Rocky Hollow, in order</a></li>
      <li><a href="#trails">Trails by difficulty</a></li>
      <li><a href="#glossary">Words the signs don't explain</a></li>
      <li><a href="#credits">Image credits</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <!-- ===== L8 · id="route" is unique — the contents list points here ===== -->
  <section id="route">
  <h2>Rocky Hollow, in order</h2>
  <p>Shuffle these and you would be walking the ladders downhill in the dark, so this
  one is ordered.</p>
  <ol>
    <li>Park at the Nature Center lot, not the inn</li>
    <li>Cross the suspension bridge over Sugar Creek</li>
    <li>Turn right into the gorge at the Trail 3 marker</li>
    <li>Climb the ladder section — both hands, no phone</li>
    <li>Follow the creek bed until it opens out at Wedge Rock</li>
    <li>Come back on Trail 5 rather than the way you came</li>
  </ol>

  </section>

  <section id="trails">
  <h2>Trails, grouped by how hard they are</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Easy
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 1 — paved, and the only one a stroller survives</li>
        <li>Trail 7 — flat, wooded, quiet on a weekday</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Moderate
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 5 — the sensible way back out of the gorge</li>
        <li>Trail 9 — long, but nothing technical</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Rugged
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 3 — ladders, creek crossings, <span class="warning">genuinely hard when wet</span></li>
        <li>Trail 10 — Bear Hollow, and usually empty for a reason</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <section id="glossary">
  <h2>Words the signs use without explaining</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt>Gorge</dt>
    <dd>A narrow canyon cut down through sandstone by the creek. Cold, and it stays
    wet days after the rain stops.</dd>

    <dt>Hemlock</dt>
    <dd>The dark evergreen growing out of the ravine walls. Left over from the last
    ice age, which is the single best fact about this park.</dd>

    <dt>Ladder section</dt>
    <dd>Steel rungs bolted straight into the rock face on Trail 3. Not optional —
    there is no way around it.</dd>
  </dl>

  </section>

  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · #top points at the id on the <h1> ===== -->
  <p><a href="#top">Back to top</a></p>

  </main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>© 2026 — Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>Indiana State Parks</title>
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== page title ===== -->
  <h1>My Site About Indiana State Parks</h1>
  <p>Welcome. This site is about the state parks in Indiana, which ones are worth
  the drive, and what you can actually do at each one.</p>

  <!-- ===== why I picked this ===== -->
  <h2>Why I picked this</h2>
  <p>My family has been going to Turkey Run since I was small, and I found out there
  are <strong>twenty-three more state parks</strong> I had never heard of. I want to
  make a page for each one I visit this year.</p>
  <p>The ones closest to Indianapolis are Fort Harrison and Shades. Both are under an
  hour, which matters when you are <em>relying on someone else to drive you</em>.</p>

  <!-- ===== what I already know ===== -->
  <h2>What I already know</h2>
  <p>Turkey Run has ladders bolted into the rock in some of the canyon trails.
  <strong>Trail 3 is genuinely hard in wet weather</strong> — that is not a warning
  the sign makes obvious enough.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite></p>

  <!-- ===== what's coming ===== -->
  <h2>What's coming</h2>
  <p>Right now this is one page with no pictures and no colors. That is on purpose.
  Structure first.</p>
  <p>By the end of this unit there will be a page for each park, a table of hours and
  fees, and a form to tell me which one to visit next.</p>

  <!-- TODO: add a page for Shades once I've been there -->

</body>
</html>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>Turkey Run — Indiana State Parks</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="images/favicon.png">
</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== page title ===== -->
  <h1>Turkey Run State Park</h1>

  <!-- ===== L7 · the nav — one list of links, identical on every page ===== -->

    <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
    <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
  </ul>

  <p>This is the park I actually know. Everything below is from walking it, not from
  the park website.</p>

  <!-- ===== L7 · an ORDERED list — the order is the whole point ===== -->
  <h2>Rocky Hollow, in order</h2>
  <p>Shuffle these and you would be walking the ladders downhill in the dark, so this
  one is ordered.</p>
  <ol>
    <li>Park at the Nature Center lot, not the inn</li>
    <li>Cross the suspension bridge over Sugar Creek</li>
    <li>Turn right into the gorge at the Trail 3 marker</li>
    <li>Climb the ladder section — both hands, no phone</li>
    <li>Follow the creek bed until it opens out at Wedge Rock</li>
    <li>Come back on Trail 5 rather than the way you came</li>
  </ol>

  <!-- ===== L7 · a NESTED list — the trails belong under their difficulty ===== -->
  <h2>Trails, grouped by how hard they are</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Easy
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 1 — paved, and the only one a stroller survives</li>
        <li>Trail 7 — flat, wooded, quiet on a weekday</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Moderate
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 5 — the sensible way back out of the gorge</li>
        <li>Trail 9 — long, but nothing technical</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Rugged
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 3 — ladders, creek crossings, genuinely hard when wet</li>
        <li>Trail 10 — Bear Hollow, and usually empty for a reason</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
  </ul>

  <!-- ===== L7 · a DESCRIPTION list — terms paired with what they mean ===== -->
  <h2>Words the signs use without explaining</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt>Gorge</dt>
    <dd>A narrow canyon cut down through sandstone by the creek. Cold, and it stays
    wet days after the rain stops.</dd>

    <dt>Hemlock</dt>
    <dd>The dark evergreen growing out of the ravine walls. Left over from the last
    ice age, which is the single best fact about this park.</dd>

    <dt>Ladder section</dt>
    <dd>Steel rungs bolted straight into the rock face on Trail 3. Not optional —
    there is no way around it.</dd>
  </dl>

<head>
  <!-- L9 · charset first. Without it, curly quotes become â€™ -->

       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing
       through it on every single page. Tab into the page to see it. ===== -->
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <header> means header. A div with id="header" only
       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->
  <header>
    <h1>About me</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About me</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main id="main">

  <!-- ===== L8 · the same "section" class as index.html — reused, not redefined ===== -->
  <section id="who">
  <h2>Who is writing this</h2>
  <p>I am a sophomore at Warren Central and I have been to exactly <strong>three</strong>
  of Indiana's twenty-four state parks. That is the whole reason this site exists — I
  want a record of the rest.</p>

  <!-- ===== second image, different page, same folder ===== -->
  <img src="images/shades-sugar-creek.jpg"
       alt="A wooded overlook at Shades State Park looking down into Sugar Creek">

  </section>

  <section id="why">
  <h2>Why this topic</h2>
  <p>Most park websites tell you the hours and the entrance fee. <span class="warning">None of them tell
  you whether the trail is worth it.</span> That is the part I am trying to write down
  while I still remember it.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite> —
  <a href="https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/" target="_blank">the official park
  listing</a></p>

  </section>

  <section id="next">
  <h2>What's next</h2>
  <p>A page for each park I actually visit, with photos once I learn how to put them in.</p>


  </section>

  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
    <li>"Sugar Creek from the Shades overlook" by
      <a href="https://www.flickr.com/people/example">M. Okonkwo</a>,
      via <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/example/12345678">Flickr</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>


  <!-- ===== L13 · entities. The four that matter, and WHY they exist. ===== -->
  <h2>One thing that caught me out</h2>
  <p>I wanted to write about the <code><table></code> tag on this page and the
  table just disappeared. The browser was reading my example as a real tag instead of
  as text.</p>
  <p>The fix is an <strong>entity</strong> — a code that stands in for a character
  the browser would otherwise treat as HTML:</p>
  <table>
    <caption>The entities I actually needed</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>I type</th><th>The page shows</th><th>Why I need it</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td><code>&lt;</code></td><td><</td><td>otherwise it starts a tag</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&gt;</code></td><td>></td><td>otherwise it ends one</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&amp;</code></td><td>&</td><td>otherwise it starts an entity</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&copy;</code></td><td>©</td><td>not on the keyboard</td></tr>
      <tr><td><code>&nbsp;</code></td><td>a space that never breaks</td><td>keeps
        “7 am” on one line</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <p>The one that surprised me is <code>&amp;</code>. To write the ampersand code
  itself I have to escape the ampersand, which felt like a trick question until I
  thought about it.</p>
</main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>© 2026 — Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>

<html lang="en">
<head>

       why the stylesheet is external instead of a style="" on every tag. -->

</head>
<body>

  <!-- ===== L13 · the skip link. First focusable thing on the page, so a
       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing
       through it on every single page. Tab into the page to see it. ===== -->

  <header>

      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main id="main">

  <p>I have been to four of Indiana's twenty-four state parks. If you know one worth
  the drive, tell me.</p>

  <!-- ===== L11 · action and method are named now and explained properly in U6.
       Nothing is submitted anywhere yet -- there is no backend until spring. ===== -->
  <form action="#" method="post">

    <!-- L11 · EVERY input gets a label, and for="" must match the input's id.
         Click the label text -- if the cursor jumps into the box, they match. -->
    <!-- L12 · required means the browser refuses to submit without it, and
         says so itself. No JavaScript written. -->
    <p>
      <label for="name">Your name</label><br>
      <input type="text" id="name" name="name"
             placeholder="First name is fine" required>
    </p>

    <!-- L12 · type="email" validates the shape AND changes the on-screen
         keyboard on a phone. type="text" does neither. -->
    <p>
      <label for="email">Email</label><br>
      <input type="email" id="email" name="email"
             placeholder="you@example.com" required>
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="visits">How many state parks have you been to?</label><br>
      <input type="number" id="visits" name="visits" min="0" max="24" value="0">
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="when">When would you go?</label><br>
      <input type="date" id="when" name="when">
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="park">Which park?</label><br>
      <select id="park" name="park">
        <option value="">-- pick one --</option>
        <option value="shades">Shades</option>
        <option value="brown-county">Brown County</option>
        <option value="clifty-falls">Clifty Falls</option>
        <option value="indiana-dunes">Indiana Dunes</option>
        <option value="other">Somewhere else</option>
      </select>
    </p>

    <p>
      <label for="why">Why that one?</label><br>
      <textarea id="why" name="why" rows="5" cols="40"></textarea>
    </p>

    <!-- L12 · a radio GROUP shares one name. Different names = they all stay
         selectable at once, which is the classic radio-button bug. -->
    <fieldset>
      <legend>How far will you drive?</legend>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="near" name="distance" value="near" checked>
        <label for="near">Under an hour</label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="mid" name="distance" value="mid">
        <label for="mid">One to three hours</label>
      </p>
      <p>
        <input type="radio" id="far" name="distance" value="far">
        <label for="far">As far as it takes</label>
      </p>
    </fieldset>

    <p>
      <input type="checkbox" id="ladders" name="ladders" value="yes">
      <label for="ladders">I am fine with ladders and creek crossings</label>
    </p>

    <p><button type="submit">Send it</button></p>

  </form>

  <!-- L12 · try submitting this empty, then with a bad email. The browser
       complains on its own -- that is built-in validation, and it is a preview
       of the real validation you write in JavaScript in the spring.
       It still goes nowhere on submit. There is no backend until U6. -->

  </main>

  <footer>
    <p>© 2026 — Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>

  <!-- ===== L8 · a classed div groups the intro. class = reusable ===== -->
  <div class="intro">
    <p>Welcome. This site is about the state parks in Indiana, which ones are worth
    the drive, and what you can actually do at each one.</p>

  <!-- ===== the hero image — relative path into the images folder ===== -->

       alt="A narrow sandstone canyon at Turkey Run with a wooden ladder bolted into the rock face">

  <!-- ===== why I picked this ===== -->
  <h2>Why I picked this</h2>
  <p>My family has been going to Turkey Run since I was small, and I found out there
  are <strong>twenty-three more state parks</strong> I had never heard of. I want to
  make a page for each one I visit this year.</p>
  <p>The ones closest to Indianapolis are Fort Harrison and Shades. Both are under an
  hour, which matters when you are <em>relying on someone else to drive you</em>.</p>

  <!-- ===== what I already know ===== -->
  <h2>What I already know</h2>
  <p>Turkey Run has ladders bolted into the rock in some of the canyon trails.
  <span class="warning">Trail 3 is genuinely hard in wet weather</span> — that is not a warning
  the sign makes obvious enough.</p>

  <blockquote>
    Rugged trails, deep sandstone ravines, and hemlock groves make Turkey Run one of
    Indiana's most scenic state parks.
  </blockquote>
  <p><cite>Indiana Department of Natural Resources</cite> —
  <a href="https://www.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/" target="_blank">the official park
  listing</a></p>

  <!-- ===== L7 · an unordered list — order carries no meaning here ===== -->
  <h2>What to take</h2>
  <p>Nothing on this list is more important than the others, so it is unordered.</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Boots you do not mind soaking — Trail 3 crosses the creek</li>
    <li>More water than you think</li>

  <p>By the end of this unit there will be a page for each park, a table of hours and

  <section id="parks">

      </tr>

  <!-- ===== L8 · same class, different content — that's what class is for ===== -->
  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
    <li>"Sugar Creek from the Shades overlook" by
      <a href="https://www.flickr.com/people/example">M. Okonkwo</a>,

      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>


  <!-- ===== L9 · an iframe embeds someone else's page inside yours. This is the
       EMBED url from Share -> Embed a map, not the one in the address bar. ===== -->
  <section id="map">
  <h2>Where Turkey Run actually is</h2>
  <p>An hour and a half from Indianapolis, in Parke County, and the last twenty
  minutes have no signal.</p>

    src="https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html?bbox=-87.22%2C39.86%2C-87.16%2C39.91&layer=mapnik"

/* ============================================================
   U2 L1 — the first stylesheet.
   ONE file. Every page links to it. Change a rule here and all
   four pages change at once — that is the whole argument for an
   EXTERNAL stylesheet over writing style="" on every element.

   A rule is a SELECTOR, then a block of property: value; pairs.
   Leave out a semicolon and the rule AFTER it breaks, not this one.
   ============================================================ */

/* --- element selector: every <body> on the site.
       A font, a colour, a line height. Nothing clever. --- */
body {
  font-family: Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
  line-height: 1.6;
  color: #222222;
  background-color: #fdfdfb;
}

/* --- element selectors: the headings --- */
h1 {
  color: #14532d;
  font-size: 2rem;
}

h2 {
  color: #14532d;
}

/* --- CLASS selector. The dot means "any element with class=intro".
       We put class="intro" on that div back in L8, for exactly this. --- */
.intro {
  background-color: #eef4ee;
}

/* --- another class, already on the page since L8 --- */
.warning {
  color: #b3261e;
  font-weight: bold;
}

/* --- ID selector. The hash means "the one element with id=parks".
       An id is unique on a page, so this styles exactly one thing. --- */
#parks {
  background-color: #ffffff;
}

/* ============================================================
   THE CASCADE — read these two rules in order.
   Both select the same links. The SECOND one wins, because when
   two rules have the same specificity the later one is applied.
   Swap them and the colour changes. That is the cascade.
   ============================================================ */
a {
  color: #7a5901;
}

a {
  color: #14532d;
}

<body>

  <!-- ===== L13 · the skip link. First focusable thing on the page, so a
       keyboard or screen-reader user can jump the nav instead of tabbing

       LOOKS like one -- to a screen reader it is an anonymous box. ===== -->

    <h1 id="top">Turkey Run State Park</h1>

    <!-- L10 · <nav> is reserved for navigation. Not every list of links. -->
    <nav>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="turkey-run.html">Turkey Run</a></li>

        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>

  <main id="main">

  <p>This is the park I actually know. Everything below is from walking it, not from
  the park website.</p>

  <!-- ===== L8 · on-page contents. A list (L7) whose links point at ids (L8) ===== -->
  <div class="contents">
    <h2>On this page</h2>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#route">Rocky Hollow, in order</a></li>
      <li><a href="#trails">Trails by difficulty</a></li>
      <li><a href="#glossary">Words the signs don't explain</a></li>
      <li><a href="#credits">Image credits</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <!-- ===== L8 · id="route" is unique — the contents list points here ===== -->
  <section id="route">
  <h2>Rocky Hollow, in order</h2>
  <p>Shuffle these and you would be walking the ladders downhill in the dark, so this
  one is ordered.</p>
  <ol>
    <li>Park at the Nature Center lot, not the inn</li>
    <li>Cross the suspension bridge over Sugar Creek</li>
    <li>Turn right into the gorge at the Trail 3 marker</li>
    <li>Climb the ladder section — both hands, no phone</li>
    <li>Follow the creek bed until it opens out at Wedge Rock</li>
    <li>Come back on Trail 5 rather than the way you came</li>
  </ol>

  </section>

  <section id="trails">
  <h2>Trails, grouped by how hard they are</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Easy
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 1 — paved, and the only one a stroller survives</li>
        <li>Trail 7 — flat, wooded, quiet on a weekday</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Moderate
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 5 — the sensible way back out of the gorge</li>
        <li>Trail 9 — long, but nothing technical</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Rugged
      <ul>
        <li>Trail 3 — ladders, creek crossings, <span class="warning">genuinely hard when wet</span></li>
        <li>Trail 10 — Bear Hollow, and usually empty for a reason</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <section id="glossary">
  <h2>Words the signs use without explaining</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt>Gorge</dt>
    <dd>A narrow canyon cut down through sandstone by the creek. Cold, and it stays
    wet days after the rain stops.</dd>

    <dt>Hemlock</dt>
    <dd>The dark evergreen growing out of the ravine walls. Left over from the last
    ice age, which is the single best fact about this park.</dd>

    <dt>Ladder section</dt>
    <dd>Steel rungs bolted straight into the rock face on Trail 3. Not optional —
    there is no way around it.</dd>
  </dl>

  </section>

  <section id="credits">
  <h2>Image credits</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>"Turkey Run State Park, Rocky Hollow" by
      <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:ExampleUser">C. Whitaker</a>,
      via <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Example.jpg">Wikimedia Commons</a>,
      licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>.
      Cropped to 3:2.</li>
  </ul>

  </section>

  <!-- ===== L8 · #top points at the id on the <h1> ===== -->
  <p><a href="#top">Back to top</a></p>

  </main>

  <!-- ===== L10 · <footer> for credits and attributions ===== -->
  <footer>
    <p>© 2026 — Built in 7185 Website and Database Development. Photographs are credited on the
    home page; text is mine.</p>
  </footer>

</body>
</html>
